builds.name: Dark Hexer
builds.description:
Dark Hexer is a devastating hex build that abuses dark orb and affinity to melt everything. Designed around high Intelligence 40, Faith 40, Vigor 20, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Dark Hexer handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Sunset Staff's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Dark Hexer is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Sunset Staff are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Dark Hexer is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

phases.areasVi: Things Betwixt, Majula, Forest of Fallen Giants
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Intelligence.
Explore Things Betwixt, Majula, Forest of Fallen Giants thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Sunset Staff or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Sorcerer weapon is adequate while you rush toward Sunset Staff.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Sunset Staff, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Choose Sorcerer for starting Soul Arrow catalyst determines your early game approach.

Designed around high Intelligence 60, Vigor 20, Endurance 10, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Pure Sorcery handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Staff of Wisdom's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Pure Sorcery is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Staff of Wisdom are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Pure Sorcery is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Intelligence.

Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Sorcerer weapon is adequate while you rush toward Staff of Wisdom.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.

Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Staff of Wisdom, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.

Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.

Silverblack Spear Dark is a dark build using the silverblack spear. Designed around high Vigor 35, Intelligence 30, Faith 30, this build achieves a easy difficulty level that welcomes newcomers while satisfying veterans.

In PvE, Silverblack Spear Dark handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Silverblack Spear's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Silverblack Spear Dark is its accessibility and consistent performance. Key items like Silverblack Spear are obtained early in the game, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should experiment with different weapons of the same class to find their preferred moveset.

Designed with newer players in mind, Silverblack Spear Dark is straightforward to assemble and play effectively from the start. Item locations are accessible early, and the playstyle doesn't demand complex input sequences or frame-perfect timing. Veterans will appreciate the raw efficiency — this build deletes content without requiring excessive setup or consumable management. Whether this is your first playthrough or your tenth, you'll find satisfaction in the consistent, reliable performance this build delivers across all content.

steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Vigor.
Explore Things Betwixt, Majula, Forest of Fallen Giants thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Silverblack Spear or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Warrior weapon is adequate while you rush toward Silverblack Spear.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Silverblack Spear, the sooner your build comes online.

Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Drangleic Castle and Shrine of Amana contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Clear optional endgame areas for their unique rewards. Hidden bosses drop some of the best items in the base game.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Vigor Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.

builds.name: Sanctum Mace STR
builds.description:
Sanctum Mace STR is a strength/faith build using the sanctum mace from the sunken king dlc. Designed around high Strength 40, Faith 40, Vigor 35, this build achieves a moderate difficulty level that rewards game knowledge and mechanical skill. The build fully utilizes DLC content, incorporating endgame weapons, spells, and talismans that significantly elevate its performance.

In PvE, Sanctum Mace STR handles every challenge with confidence. Boss fights become a dance of positioning and timing as you leverage the Sanctum Mace's unique properties. Regular enemies and area traversal feel smooth thanks to the balanced stat investment — you have enough damage to clear trash efficiently and enough Vigor to survive surprises. The build prioritizes sustainable damage output through its primary stat while maintaining the defensive stats needed to learn new boss patterns without frustration.

The core strength of Sanctum Mace STR is its versatility and damage potential when optimized. Key items like Sanctum Mace are acquired through mid-game progression or specific questlines, allowing the build to come online at a reasonable point. The primary weakness is occasional reliance on specific items or buffs — maintaining uptime requires attention. Players should practice the core combos regularly to build muscle memory.

Sanctum Mace STR is ideal for players who have completed at least one playthrough and want to explore a different approach to combat. It rewards game knowledge — knowing where key items are, which bosses to tackle in order, and how to optimize your route makes a significant difference. While the core build functions with basic items, reaching its full potential requires exploring optional areas, completing specific NPC questlines, and understanding soft cap breakpoints for efficient leveling.

phases.name: Early Game
steps: Prioritize leveling Vigor/Vitality to comfortable levels before investing heavily in damage stats — survival comes first in the early game, aim for 20 Vigor before focusing on Strength.
Explore Things Betwixt, Majula, Forest of Fallen Giants thoroughly. Each cave, catacomb, and ruin contains valuable upgrade materials, spells, and consumables crucial for progression.
Talk to every NPC you encounter — many offer questlines that reward essential items like Sanctum Mace or key upgrade materials later. Never attack NPCs unless you know their drops.
Save Smithing Stones and upgrade materials for weapons you'll use long-term. Your starting Cleric weapon is adequate while you rush toward Sanctum Mace.
Purchase a backup weapon from a merchant — having a Strike weapon for crystal/skeleton enemies and a Thrust weapon for armored foes covers all resistances.
Master your weapon's moveset in early areas. Practice spacing on basic soldiers, roll timing against large enemies, and learn which attacks have poise/hyper armor.
Summon NPC phantoms for tough early bosses if needed. Many games hide summon signs near boss fogs — the game expects you to use them.
Collect every flask upgrade item — Golden Seeds, Estus Shards, Sacred Tears. Each upgrade provides more value than several stat points for survival.
Revisit merchants after major story progression — they often stock new items, spells, or unlimited upgrade materials after key milestones.
Rush toward your build's defining weapon early. Run past enemies if necessary — the sooner you get Sanctum Mace, the sooner your build comes online.
Kill every optional boss and mini-boss you encounter. They drop unique weapons, talismans, and valuable souls/runes for early leveling.
Buy basic spells (Glintstone Pebble equivalent) from early vendors. Even weak spells are excellent for clearing trash packs and pulling enemies from safe range.
Keep Endurance/Stamina at comfortable levels (15-20 early). An extra swing or roll often means the difference between winning and dying.
Experiment with Weapon Arts / Skills early. The Pick Cleric for Faith start determines your early game approach.
Check the Whetblade / Infusion item availability. Changing weapon affinity early lets you scale with your primary damage stat from the start.

phases.name: Mid Game
steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Strength should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Sanctum Mace, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Lost Bastille and Huntsman's Copse have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Strength investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Strength-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Iron Keep and Shaded Woods contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like spell slots, faster casting, or damage buffs at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Find the best catalyst/seal/staff for your build. Dragon Communion Seal and Prince of Death's Staff provide hybrid scaling.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.

Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Huntsman's Copse bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

phases.name: Late Game
steps: Push Strength to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. The 55/55 split for Quality or 80 for pure physical provides optimal AR.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Drangleic Castle and Shrine of Amana contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Sanctum Mace.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Strength Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Use Terra Magicus / Steady Chant / Magic-boosting physick before boss doors. Buffing before entering maximizes your burst damage windows.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Undead Crypt and Dragon Shrine bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Strength-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Attune a diverse spell loadout. Ranged projectiles for approach, AoE for crowds, buffs for bosses, and utility spells for exploration cover all scenarios.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

steps: Reach your weapon's stat requirements to unlock its full potential. Dexterity should be your primary focus, with secondary investment in supporting stats.
Complete NPC questlines tied to your build. Many reward Poison Dagger x2, powerful talismans, or unique spells. Check in with quest givers after each major boss.
Farm upgrade materials from specific mid-game enemies. Lost Bastille and Huntsman's Copse have excellent farming spots for Chunks and upgrade materials.
Consider respeccing if your stats are suboptimal. Most games offer respec items (Larval Tear, Soul Vessel) — use them to fine-tune your Dexterity investment.
Equip talismans/rings that synergize with your damage type. Dexterity-boosting talismans (Scorpion Charms, Clutch Rings, Firstborn Rings) provide significant multipliers.
Explore optional areas before pushing main story progression. Iron Keep and Shaded Woods contain vital mid-game pickups for your build.
Join a covenant aligned with your playstyle. Many offer rewards like bonus damage, HP regen, or unique weapons at rank milestones.
Invest in Mind/FP or Attunement if your build uses skills or spells. Running out of FP mid-fight is a common and preventable cause of death.
Infuse your weapon with Dexterity affinity. Heavy/Sharp/Quality inflections maximize AR at higher stat levels.
Practice your core combat loop against mid-game enemies. Learn boss punish windows and optimal damage combos for your weapon class.
Collect respec items and keep them for emergencies. Having 2-3 respecs available lets you experiment with different stat distributions.
Target 35-40 Vigor/Vitality by mid-game. Weapon upgrade level contributes more to damage than raw stats at this stage — invest in survival first.
Maintain medium roll (under 70% equip load) at minimum. Fast roll (under 30%) is ideal for lighter builds. Defense and poise protect more than fashion.
Use consumables matching boss weaknesses. Huntsman's Copse bosses are particularly vulnerable to specific damage types — prepare accordingly.
Stockpile crafting materials. Resins, spell buffs, and consumables for your damage type provide 15-30% DPS increases that scale with your upgrades.

steps: Push Dexterity to the soft cap for maximum damage scaling. The 55/55 split for Quality or 80 for pure physical provides optimal AR.
Max your primary weapon to the highest upgrade level. Every level at high stat investment provides significant AR increases — check for Somber/Regular upgrade paths.
Farm the best talismans/rings/gems from endgame areas. Drangleic Castle and Shrine of Amana contain S-tier upgrades that transform your build's power.
Complete the DLC content before the final boss. DLC areas contain some of the game's best weapons, talismans, and spells — including direct upgrades for Poison Dagger x2.
Stack multiplicative damage bonuses. Dexterity Scorpion Charm, Clutch Ring, or covenant rings combined with skill damage talismans provide exponential returns.
Apply weapon buffs matching boss weaknesses. Fire Paper for beasts, Lightning for dragons, Magic for heavily armored foes.
Learn endgame boss patterns through repetition. Undead Crypt and Dragon Shrine bosses have complex mix-ups — patience during first attempts pays off.
Optimize flask allocation per boss. Hard-hitting bosses demand more healing flasks, while spell-heavy builds should prioritize FP flasks for sustained damage.
Customize your Physick/Wondrous Elixir for each fight. Dexterity-boosting tears combined with damage-negation tears cover offense and defense simultaneously.
Carry backup weapons with different damage types. A Strike weapon, a Standard weapon, and an elemental option handle any resistance profile.
Upgrade a secondary weapon to +9/+24 minimum. Status-infused backup weapons (Bleed, Frost, Poison) or different movesets give options against resistant bosses.
Aim for poise breakpoints if your build supports it. 51+ poise in Elden Ring, 40+ in DS3, or max poise in DS1 lets you trade through enemy attacks.
Equip the strongest defensive talisman available. Dragoncrest Greatshield / Steel Protection +3 provides 20% physical damage reduction — a massive effective HP boost.
Test your build against optional superbosses before the final encounter. If you can handle the hardest optional boss, the final boss is manageable.
Record your damage numbers before and after optimization. Understanding the difference between 60% optimization and 95% optimization helps prioritize remaining upgrades.

tips: Poison in DS2 deals 1000 total damage — enough to win the attrition war
The Rat Ring extends poison duration by 50%
You can proc poison on most bosses in 2-3 powerstance L1 combos
Keep a backup Lightning weapon for enemies immune to poison
Sanctum Crossbow Poison Bolts poison in 2-3 hits from range
Meme builds like Poison Master are about having fun. Don't worry about optimization — enjoy the unique playstyle and surprise factor.
Level Adaptability until your Agility (AGL) reaches 105 — this gives you maximum iframes on rolls. For Poison Master, this is non-negotiable.
Lifegems are cheap and stackable healing items. Always carry 99 for chipping damage recovery — they save Estus for emergencies.
Enemy despawns after 12 kills in an area. Join Company of Champions to prevent despawns while farming titanite and equipment.
Bonfire Ascetics respawn the area boss and all enemies at NG+ difficulty. Use them on the Rotten for easy souls and rare drops.
Powerstance requires 1.5x the weapon's stat requirements. Consider powerstancing two weapons of the same class for bonus damage.
The Stone Ring is essential for stagger — without it, lighter weapons bounce off heavily armored enemies in DLC areas.
